TempleInfo.aboutDescription: Founded on the sacred grounds of Mallakam in the Jaffna peninsula, the Neeliyampathi Pillaiyar Kovil stands as a beacon of spiritual heritage and devotion. Our temple is a sacred sanctuary where the divine presence of Lord Pillaiyar blesses all who enter through its hallowed archway.
TempleInfo.aboutQuote: Like a lotus of Realised divine glory of Ganapathy – Mallakam temple is a spiritual fortress that has stood the test of time, nurturing generations of devotees.
TempleInfo.history: With centuries of unbroken tradition, this temple has been the spiritual heart of Mallakam, witnessing and nurturing the faith of countless families across generations.

TempleHistory.title: History of Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple
TempleHistory.intro: The temple situated in Neeliyampanai, Mallakam, once known by the special name Kulakkarai Pillaiyar, stands as a sacred place surrounded by several ancient temples that reflect the rich heritage of the region.

location.title: The Location and Spiritual Significance of Neeliyampanai
paragraphs: The temple situated in Neeliyampanai, Mallakam, was once known by the special name Kulakkarai Pillaiyar. The temple is surrounded on all four sides by four prominent temples that represent the ancient heritage of the region. Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar stands at the centre adjoining the fertile agricultural land, while the Sivagnana Vairavar Temple lies to the north, the Sri Pathirakali Amman Temple to the east, the Veerabhathirar Temple to the southeast, and the Periyanayaki Thayar Sametha Periyathambiran Temple to the west.

Mallakam is situated in the Valikamam North region of the Jaffna peninsula, an area blessed with abundant water resources and fertile agricultural lands. The village has long held a prominent place in the worship of Lord Ganesha, known as Ganapathyam. The southern part of Mallakam, where the Saivite community has traditionally lived, is surrounded by ponds, coconut groves, and expansive paddy fields, creating a peaceful landscape of natural beauty. Neeliyampanai is situated within this serene environment.

Surrounded by groves shaded by sacred fig and banyan trees, Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple stands as a place where devotees seek the fulfilment of their prayers and receive divine grace. The people living in the surrounding area have a deep devotion to Lord Pillaiyar and regard Him with the affection and love of a mother.

nameOrigin.title: The Origin of the Name Neeliyampanai
paragraphs: In ancient times, people often gave places meaningful names based on characteristics that were closely associated with the particular location.

The name Neeli refers to medicinal plants and vegetation associated with blue-coloured flowers and seeds, including the Neeli medicinal plant, Maruthondri tree, and Karuppuk Kodi. These were considered valuable medicinal plants and were once found abundantly in this water-rich region.

Even today, although the Neeli medicinal plant and Karuththa Kodi have become rare due to natural changes and human activity, they can still be found in a few places. The large pond situated to the south of the Pillaiyar Temple was once known to contain blue water-lily plants.

When the temple pond was deepened in 1950, some of these aquatic plants disappeared. This is believed to be one of the reasons why the deity worshipped here came to be known as Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar. Since the temple is also situated beside the pond, our ancestors also referred to the deity as Kulakkarai Pillaiyar, a name that continues to be used today.

earlyHistory.title: The Early History of the Temple
paragraphs: The stone image of Lord Ganesha, which is believed to have been worshipped in an aniconic form beneath a tree in the area surrounding the present outer courtyard of the temple, was placed there and worshipped by the people of the region. This may have been from a period before the 18th century.

There is also an oral tradition that the ancestors of the people living in this area established a place of worship for Lord Ganesha after witnessing the miraculous emergence of a spring at the location where the temple pond is situated today.

Regardless of the exact circumstances, during the 16th and 17th centuries, when foreign rule was characterised by a lack of religious tolerance, Saivite Tamil people did not have the freedom to openly build temples and worship. Existing stone temples were also destroyed by the foreign rulers.
Therefore, it is believed that the people of Neeliyampanai worshipped Lord Ganesha by placing the deity beneath a tree during that period.

sindhamaniEra.title: 1850 to 1962 — The Development of the Temple
paragraphs: From 1850 onwards, the history of Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple becomes much more clearly documented. When discussing the origin and development of the temple, it is important to recognise the contributions of Thiruvatti Ramalingam Ponnu Amma and her son, Mr. E. Chinthamani.

A devoted worshipper of Lord Pillaiyar who lived in this area, Thiruvatti Ramalingam Ponnu Amma established a small shrine for Lord Ganesha beneath a poovarasu tree on the present temple land. As religious tolerance existed under British rule, she was able to worship the deity openly and performed daily worship and pujas with great devotion.

As a result of her deep devotion, on 19 November 1880, Lord Ganesha blessed Thiruvatti Ramalingam Ponnu Amma with a son. He was Mr. E. Chinthamani, who later became one of the most important figures in the development of the temple.
From around 1900 to 1960, Mr. Thillaiyambalam and several other devotees worked closely with Mr. Chinthamani for almost half a century, dedicating themselves to the development of the temple.

Among those who supported the temple were Kanagasabapaththa, affectionately known as Mr. Kanagasabai, Mr. Saravanamuthu, Mr. Kandiah, the second festival sponsor, Mr. Subramaniam, father of Mr. Sivanandan who later served as a Government Agent, and Mr. R. N. Sivapirakasam, a renowned Tamil scholar and Saiva Siddhanta scholar who was also a lawyer at the time. These individuals contributed to the temple while also carrying out important responsibilities in government and public service.

Mr. E. Chinthamani was a highly educated person who held significant responsibilities in administration. The British Government of Ceylon recognised his administrative service by awarding him the honour O.B.E. In addition to his administrative abilities, he was deeply devoted to God.

The history of Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple cannot be separated from the life and service of Mr. E. Chinthamani. He dedicated approximately 60 years to the administration and development of the temple. Although people faced financial difficulties during that period, they responded positively to his requests and provided their support.

After the temple was established according to Agamic principles, Mr. Chinthamani made a significant contribution towards providing the temple priest with a monthly salary. In 1946, he also built the temple's Vasantha Mandapam.
Following his mother's request that the temple priest should live close to the temple, he built a permanent house for the priest at his own expense in 1950 on the western side of the temple.

When the temple required financial assistance, he mortgaged his own land situated on the western boundary of what is now known as Brahmana Valavu and provided funds for the construction and development of the temple.

Mr. E. Chinthamani passed away on 14 February 1962. After his death, the land became part of his children's inheritance. His children and their spouses jointly settled the amount and transferred the land to the temple.
All temple festivals were organised by Mr. E. Chinthamani. Mr. K. Suppiah and Mr. Vai. Ganapathipillai also worked alongside him in carrying out the responsibilities of the temple.
Through his lifelong dedication and service, Mr. Chinthamani demonstrated that one person, through devotion and determination, could make a lasting contribution to the growth of the temple.

thillaiyambalamEra.title: The Contributions of Mr. V. Thillaiyambalam
paragraphs: Several important historical events marked the development of Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple. Recording these events is valuable for those who wish to understand the early history of the temple and for future generations.

Mr. V. Thillaiyambalam played a significant role in constructing the temple according to Agamic principles. He was a wealthy and respected member of the Neeliyampanai community during the first quarter of the 20th century. He had great love and devotion towards Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar and dedicated himself to the service of the temple.

The temple originally existed as a small monastery or shrine. The construction and development of the present temple, from the sanctum sanctorum to the Artha Mandapam, Maha Mandapam and Sthamba Mandapam, was carried out through the dedicated contributions of both Mr. E. Chinthamani and Mr. V. Thillaiyambalam.
The mandapams were constructed between approximately 1917 and 1927. There is also a tradition that the construction took place during the broader period between 1900 and 1927.

As one of his major contributions, Mr. Thillaiyambalam established the temple flagstaff and constructed the Sthamba Mandapam that can still be seen today. During the same period, he also helped establish the annual Maha Utsavam of the temple.

According to his grandchildren, the flagstaff was installed sometime between 1917 and 1927. From the beginning of the festival sponsorship by Mr. Thillaiyambalam, his descendants have continued to honour the tradition of sponsoring and conducting the flag-hoisting festival.

landDonations.title: Land Donations to the Temple
paragraphs: Several members of earlier generations made significant contributions to the development of the temple. These devotees donated land to Lord Ganesha as acts of charity, and as a result, the temple acquired the surrounding land that today includes the Annadana Hall and the temple roads.
The ancestors of the family who are currently associated with the second festival sponsorship donated their land situated along the western side of the temple road to the temple.
The ancestors of the family associated with the sixth festival sponsorship donated the land on which the present ceremonial bathing well and the sanctum sanctorum are situated.
The ancestors of the family associated with the ninth festival sponsorship donated the land containing the present Madappalli and its accompanying well.

Among other individuals who donated land to the temple was Mr. Saravanamuthu, the father of Mrs. Janaki Kumaraswamy and a relative of Mr. Chinthamani. He donated the land situated along the southern and western temple roads.

In order to widen the southern temple road, prevent the temple road from becoming restricted as a public pathway, and provide sufficient space for the deity's procession around the temple, additional land was donated along the road boundary. This was done following requests from festival sponsors Mr. Suppiah and Mr. Sivathondan and later at the request of Mr. Kandhasamy, who served as chairman of the administration committee from 2000 to 2011. The land was donated first by Mrs. Kanagasabapathy Maheswari and later by her son Mr. K. Thamotharampillai.

chariotAndAdministration.title: 1950 to 1980 — The Chariot and Temple Administration
paragraphs: During the 1950s, work began on constructing a new temple chariot. The work was undertaken by Mr. Thambipillai, a member of the Visvakarma community who was renowned at the time for his expertise in traditional sculptural craftsmanship.

Mr. Thambipillai also carried out the traditional work of providing the supporting wooden structure used for positioning and securing the chariot. From the time the chariot was first put into use until today, this traditional responsibility has continued to be carried out by members of his family lineage.

Following the death of Mr. E. Chinthamani in 1962, the administration of the temple was carried out under the leadership of his son, Mr. Chockanathan, with Mr. E. Suppiah serving as an assistant together with other devotees involved in temple activities.
An administration committee headed by Mr. K. Sivathondan was elected around 1977. Mr. K. Sivathondan served as the chairman of the temple administration committee during the 1970s and until 1980.

During this period, devotees including Mr. C. Chockanathan, Mr. E. Sivanesan, Mr. K. Thiyagarajah, Mr. S. Arasathungam and Mr. Mudisingarajah supported the administration and contributed to the temple's activities.

Several important renovation works were undertaken during this period. The southern section of the inner temple courtyard, which had previously been covered with a simple earthen surface, was converted into a cemented stone floor. The stone pillars that can be seen around the inner courtyard today were also constructed during this period.
A strong permanent tiled roof supported by pillars was subsequently constructed around three sides of the inner courtyard.
Following the completion of the renovation work to the inner courtyard, the Mahakumbabhishekam of Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple was held on 1 May 1980.
During this period of administration, the families who worshipped at Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple continued to contribute towards the monthly salary of the temple priest.

The Tiruvathavur Adigal Puranam recitation also continued during this period, particularly during the Margazhi Thiruvempavai season. Mr. Suppiah and Mr. Arasathungam took a strong interest in ensuring that the Puranam recitation was conducted properly.

It is recorded that the Puranam recitation and explanation continued until around 1980. The devotees of that period participated with great interest and devotion, listening to and experiencing the recitations.

1992To2002.title: 1992 to 2002 — A Challenging Period and Temple Restoration
paragraphs: At the temple's general meeting held in 1992, an administration committee was formed under the leadership of Mr. E. Kathirkamalingam. He served as the chairman of the temple administration from 1992 and again from 23 November 1997 until 18 December 2002.
During this period, the administration committee had to face many challenges caused by the difficult and unstable circumstances prevailing in the country.

In October 1995, Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple, its surrounding area and the people of the Jaffna region experienced an extremely difficult period. Like many other people in Jaffna, the residents of Neeliyampanai were forced to leave their homes and become displaced.
Mr. Kumarasamy Sarma, who had faithfully performed the temple's daily religious duties for approximately four decades, was also forced to leave the temple during this painful period.
After enduring many hardships, travelling through difficult conditions and living in temporary settlements, the people gradually returned and resettled in and around the temple area.
After returning, priority was given to cleaning and restoring the temple and its surroundings and to ensuring that the daily pujas and religious activities of the temple could continue.

Mr. Kathirkamalingam again served as chairman of the administration committee from 23 November 1997 to 18 December 2002. Together with the administration committee, he worked to restore the temple from the damage and difficulties caused during this extremely challenging period.
The western and northern sections of the inner courtyard floor, which had remained incomplete from earlier renovation work, were completed with cement flooring during this period.
The old Vasantha Mandapam was also removed and the present Vasantha Mandapam was constructed with the full support and contribution of the temple volunteers.
In 1998, renovation work continued under his leadership, and following the completion of these works, the Mahakumbabhishekam of the temple was held on 31 March 1999.

Through his efforts, an assessment report concerning the damage suffered by the temple was submitted to the Northern Fisheries Settlement and Rehabilitation Authority. Based on the application submitted, the authority approved financial assistance of Rs. 331,500, which was provided in three instalments for the restoration work of the temple.

The administration committee and the people also faced difficulties during the period when the temple and its surroundings were used as camps and residential facilities by the security forces. Despite these challenges, the administration committee and devotees continued their efforts and moved forward with the development of the temple.
Mr. Kathirkamalingam's administrative ability and his strong commitment to truth, integrity and righteous conduct guided him in carrying out his responsibilities even during this difficult period.

2003To2011.title: 2003 to 2011 — Temple Development and New Contributions
paragraphs: From 19 December 2002 until 2011, Mr. K. Kandhasamy, a retired former Grama Sevaka, served as the chairman of the Dharmakartha Sabha of Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple and carried out the affairs of the temple.
During the early period of his administration, the war situation in the Northern Province gradually changed, and improved transportation facilities and greater stability began to emerge.

The previous administration and Mr. K. Kandhasamy faced considerable difficulties in appointing permanent priests for the temple. Finding priests who could provide dedicated service to the temple, similar to the earlier priests such as Mr. Kumaraswamy Sarma and the learned Mr. Mahalingam Iyer, proved to be a significant challenge.

Two important development projects were completed during his administration. Since there was insufficient space to provide daily alms during the annual Maha Utsavam, efforts were made to construct a permanent Annadana Hall.
The Annadana Hall situated along the western temple road was completed through the efforts of the administration committee.

The devotees of Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple willingly contributed the required funds towards the construction of the hall. Many elders supported the project not only through financial contributions but also through physical labour and service.

One of the major renovation projects undertaken during this administration was the construction of the Ther Mutti, a permanent structure for keeping the temple chariot. It was constructed in August 2005 as an offering by the sons of Mrs. Kanagamma Varadarasa.
Another major achievement of this administration was the construction of a new decorated temple chariot. The ceremonial first outing, or Vellottam, of the new chariot took place on 5 August 2005.
During the same period, through the efforts of the administration committee, a house was purchased for the temple priest. This residence is the house currently used by the temple priest.

2011To2013.title: 2011 to 2013 — Temple Renovation and the Mahakumbabhishekam
paragraphs: At the temple's general meeting held in 2011, a new Dharmakartha Sabha was elected. Mr. K. Thiyagarajah was elected as the chairman of the new administration committee.

Under his leadership, comprehensive renovation work was undertaken at the temple. The administration worked to restore and improve the temple while preserving its traditional religious and architectural character.
Renovation work was carried out on the sanctum sanctorum, Artha Mandapam, Maha Mandapam and other important areas of the temple. Work was also undertaken to improve the temple's Vimanam.
A beautiful three-tier Vimanam was constructed above the sanctum sanctorum. The sculptural work of the Vimanam further enhanced the spiritual and artistic character of the temple.
Necessary restoration and improvement work was carried out throughout the temple, while facilities required for devotees and for the successful conduct of the temple festivals were also improved.
Devotees, sponsors and families associated with Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple contributed financially and through voluntary labour towards these renovation projects.
Through the continuous efforts of the administration committee and the support of the devotees, the renovation work of the temple was successfully completed.

The temple, which had developed over many generations through the dedication of numerous devotees and community leaders, gained a renewed appearance while continuing to preserve its spiritual traditions.
The Mahakumbabhishekam of the temple was conducted successfully in 2013. This Mahakumbabhishekam became an important milestone in the history of Neeliyampanai Pillaiyar Temple.
The spiritual traditions and worship practices preserved by generations of devotees continue to be maintained, with the responsibility of carrying this heritage forward to future generations.
